messages.content: Explain how splitting one language model across two computers differs from running two independent models. Use three short sentences.

runs.text: Splitting a single model distributes its weights across two machines to run one unified system, whereas running two independent models creates two separate systems with distinct parameters. The split model shares a single knowledge base and produces consistent outputs, while independent models operate as separate entities that may generate different results. This approach optimizes hardware utilization for one task, unlike parallel independent runs which process two completely separate tasks simultaneously.
